+//! #3642: the letter codes an indexable insert designation is built
+//! from - shape, clearance, tolerance class and fixing - as typed
+//! values with their letters. Our own tables of the code meanings that
+//! the ISO 1832 designation system publishes and that tool vendors
+//! print in their catalogs; no standard text is copied.
+
+/// Position 1: the insert's shape, read by its corner angle.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
+pub enum InsertShape {
+    /// Parallelogram, 85 degrees.
+    A,
+    /// Parallelogram, 82 degrees.
+    B,
+    /// Rhombic, 80 degrees.
+    C,
+    /// Rhombic, 55 degrees.
+    D,
+    /// Rhombic, 75 degrees.
+    E,
+    /// Hexagon, 120 degrees.
+    H,
+    /// Parallelogram, 55 degrees.
+    K,
+    /// Rectangle, 90 degrees.
+    L,
+    /// Rhombic, 86 degrees.
+    M,
+    /// Octagon, 135 degrees.
+    O,
+    /// Pentagon, 108 degrees.
+    P,
+    /// Round.
+    R,
+    /// Square, 90 degrees.
+    S,
+    /// Triangle, 60 degrees.
+    T,
+    /// Rhombic, 35 degrees.
+    V,
+    /// Trigon, 80 degrees.
+    W,
+}
+
+/// The shape letters in one place, for the parsers' refusals.
+pub const SHAPE_LETTERS: &str = "A B C D E H K L M O P R S T V W";
+
+impl InsertShape {
+    /// The shape for its letter; `None` for a letter that is not one.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn from_letter(c: char) -> Option<Self> {
+        Some(match c {
+            'A' => Self::A,
+            'B' => Self::B,
+            'C' => Self::C,
+            'D' => Self::D,
+            'E' => Self::E,
+            'H' => Self::H,
+            'K' => Self::K,
+            'L' => Self::L,
+            'M' => Self::M,
+            'O' => Self::O,
+            'P' => Self::P,
+            'R' => Self::R,
+            'S' => Self::S,
+            'T' => Self::T,
+            'V' => Self::V,
+            'W' => Self::W,
+            _ => return None,
+        })
+    }
+
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn letter(self) -> char {
+        match self {
+            Self::A => 'A',
+            Self::B => 'B',
+            Self::C => 'C',
+            Self::D => 'D',
+            Self::E => 'E',
+            Self::H => 'H',
+            Self::K => 'K',
+            Self::L => 'L',
+            Self::M => 'M',
+            Self::O => 'O',
+            Self::P => 'P',
+            Self::R => 'R',
+            Self::S => 'S',
+            Self::T => 'T',
+            Self::V => 'V',
+            Self::W => 'W',
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The corner angle in degrees; `None` for a round insert.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn corner_deg(self) -> Option<f64> {
+        Some(match self {
+            Self::A => 85.0,
+            Self::B => 82.0,
+            Self::C | Self::W => 80.0,
+            Self::D | Self::K => 55.0,
+            Self::E => 75.0,
+            Self::H => 120.0,
+            Self::L | Self::S => 90.0,
+            Self::M => 86.0,
+            Self::O => 135.0,
+            Self::P => 108.0,
+            Self::T => 60.0,
+            Self::V => 35.0,
+            Self::R => return None,
+        })
+    }
+
+    /// The edge length over the inscribed circle's diameter, for the
+    /// shapes whose every edge touches that circle. Each edge is the
+    /// two tangent lengths from its end corners, `r / tan(a / 2)`. A
+    /// trigon alternates 80 and 160 degree corners. `None` for a
+    /// parallelogram or a rectangle (no circle touches all four
+    /// edges) and for a round insert (its size is its diameter).
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn edge_per_ic(self) -> Option<f64> {
+        let cot_half = |deg: f64| 1.0 / (deg.to_radians() * 0.5).tan();
+        // The edge in units of the radius, halved to units of the diameter.
+        let per_r = match self {
+            Self::C | Self::D | Self::E | Self::M | Self::V => {
+                let a = self.corner_deg()?;
+                cot_half(a) + cot_half(180.0 - a)
+            }
+            Self::S | Self::T | Self::H | Self::O | Self::P => 2.0 * cot_half(self.corner_deg()?),
+            Self::W => cot_half(80.0) + cot_half(160.0),
+            Self::A | Self::B | Self::K | Self::L | Self::R => return None,
+        };
+        Some(per_r * 0.5)
+    }
+}
+
+/// Position 2 (and position 4 of a holder): the clearance angle under
+/// the cutting edge.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
+pub enum Clearance {
+    A,
+    B,
+    C,
+    D,
+    E,
+    F,
+    G,
+    N,
+    P,
+    /// Another clearance, stated in the catalog.
+    O,
+}
+
+pub const CLEARANCE_LETTERS: &str = "A B C D E F G N P O";
+
+impl Clearance {
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn from_letter(c: char) -> Option<Self> {
+        Some(match c {
+            'A' => Self::A,
+            'B' => Self::B,
+            'C' => Self::C,
+            'D' => Self::D,
+            'E' => Self::E,
+            'F' => Self::F,
+            'G' => Self::G,
+            'N' => Self::N,
+            'P' => Self::P,
+            'O' => Self::O,
+            _ => return None,
+        })
+    }
+
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn letter(self) -> char {
+        match self {
+            Self::A => 'A',
+            Self::B => 'B',
+            Self::C => 'C',
+            Self::D => 'D',
+            Self::E => 'E',
+            Self::F => 'F',
+            Self::G => 'G',
+            Self::N => 'N',
+            Self::P => 'P',
+            Self::O => 'O',
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The angle in degrees; `None` for "another clearance".
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn degrees(self) -> Option<f64> {
+        Some(match self {
+            Self::A => 3.0,
+            Self::B => 5.0,
+            Self::C => 7.0,
+            Self::D => 15.0,
+            Self::E => 20.0,
+            Self::F => 25.0,
+            Self::G => 30.0,
+            Self::N => 0.0,
+            Self::P => 11.0,
+            Self::O => return None,
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+/// Position 3: the tolerance class letters. Kept as its letter: no
+/// fit check reads it.
+pub const TOLERANCE_LETTERS: &str = "A C E F G H J K L M N U";
+
+/// Position 4: how the insert is held and whether it has a chip
+/// breaker - the fixing hole is what a holder's clamping must match.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
+pub enum Fixing {
+    /// No hole, no chip breaker.
+    N,
+    /// No hole, chip breaker on one face.
+    R,
+    /// No hole, chip breakers on both faces.
+    F,
+    /// Cylindrical hole, no chip breaker.
+    A,
+    /// Cylindrical hole, chip breaker on one face.
+    M,
+    /// Cylindrical hole, chip breakers on both faces.
+    G,
+    /// Hole countersunk on one face (40-60 degrees), no chip breaker.
+    W,
+    /// Hole countersunk on one face (40-60 degrees), chip breaker.
+    T,
+    /// Hole countersunk on both faces (40-60 degrees), no chip breaker.
+    Q,
+    /// Hole countersunk on both faces (40-60 degrees), chip breakers.
+    U,
+    /// Hole countersunk on one face (70-90 degrees), no chip breaker.
+    B,
+    /// Hole countersunk on one face (70-90 degrees), chip breaker.
+    H,
+    /// Hole countersunk on both faces (70-90 degrees), no chip breaker.
+    C,
+    /// Hole countersunk on both faces (70-90 degrees), chip breakers.
+    J,
+    /// A special form, stated in the catalog.
+    X,
+}
+
+pub const FIXING_LETTERS: &str = "N R F A M G W T Q U B H C J X";
+
+/// What holds the insert in place, as a clamp reads it.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
+pub enum FixingHole {
+    /// A plain insert: a clamp from the top holds it.
+    None,
+    /// A straight hole: a pin or lever pulls it into the pocket.
+    Cylindrical,
+    /// A countersunk hole: a screw holds it.
+    Countersunk,
+    /// A special form: no standard clamp takes it.
+    Special,
+}
+
+impl Fixing {
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn from_letter(c: char) -> Option<Self> {
+        Some(match c {
+            'N' => Self::N,
+            'R' => Self::R,
+            'F' => Self::F,
+            'A' => Self::A,
+            'M' => Self::M,
+            'G' => Self::G,
+            'W' => Self::W,
+            'T' => Self::T,
+            'Q' => Self::Q,
+            'U' => Self::U,
+            'B' => Self::B,
+            'H' => Self::H,
+            'C' => Self::C,
+            'J' => Self::J,
+            'X' => Self::X,
+            _ => return None,
+        })
+    }
+
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn letter(self) -> char {
+        match self {
+            Self::N => 'N',
+            Self::R => 'R',
+            Self::F => 'F',
+            Self::A => 'A',
+            Self::M => 'M',
+            Self::G => 'G',
+            Self::W => 'W',
+            Self::T => 'T',
+            Self::Q => 'Q',
+            Self::U => 'U',
+            Self::B => 'B',
+            Self::H => 'H',
+            Self::C => 'C',
+            Self::J => 'J',
+            Self::X => 'X',
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The hole that the clamp must match.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn hole(self) -> FixingHole {
+        match self {
+            Self::N | Self::R | Self::F => FixingHole::None,
+            Self::A | Self::M | Self::G => FixingHole::Cylindrical,
+            Self::W | Self::T | Self::Q | Self::U | Self::B | Self::H | Self::C | Self::J => FixingHole::Countersunk,
+            Self::X => FixingHole::Special,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// The cutting direction of an insert or a holder.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
+pub enum Hand {
+    R,
+    L,
+    /// Neutral: cuts in both directions.
+    N,
+}
+
+impl Hand {
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn from_letter(c: char) -> Option<Self> {
+        Some(match c {
+            'R' => Self::R,
+            'L' => Self::L,
+            'N' => Self::N,
+            _ => return None,
+        })
+    }
+
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn letter(self) -> char {
+        match self {
+            Self::R => 'R',
+            Self::L => 'L',
+            Self::N => 'N',
+        }
+    }
+}

+## #3642 - Tool components: the ISO 13399 model, the insert and holder codes, and the fit checks
+
+**What was decided.**
+- The model is pure data in `camcraft-tools`, in six files:
+  `insert_codes.rs` (the letter tables), `insert_iso1832.rs` (the insert
+  code), `insert_seat.rs` (the seat and the ISO 5608 holder code),
+  `connection_code.rs`, `component.rs` and `component_fit.rs`. There is no
+  new crate edge, no ECS and no file I/O.
+- `ToolComponent::new` checks a component when it is made. The fields are
+  private, so a component that exists is valid. The id is a plain string;
+  #3644 and #3645 decide how ids are made and stored.
+- Validation rule (#4096 review): a component checks each value that
+  it is given, also the values built in code. `InsertSpec` and
+  `InsertSeatSpec` keep their public fields (the parsers and the
+  stacked #3643 build them), and each has a `check()`. `InsertSpec::check`
+  refuses a tolerance letter off the table or in lower case, a size off
+  01 to 99, a corner that the shape cannot have, a suffix character that
+  the parser changes or refuses, and a hand that the suffix does not
+  state. Then it confirms that the value is the parse of its own text,
+  which closes the whole class. `InsertSeatSpec::check` refuses an
+  insert size off 01 to 99; its letters, its style and its thickness are
+  types that hold only valid values. `ToolComponent::new` runs both
+  checks and names the component, the seat port and the position.
+  `check_insert_fit` runs them again as a guard.
+- Connections are normalized, not refused: `ConnectionCode::canonical()`
+  is the value that the code's text parses to (`Hsk { form: 'a' }` is
+  `HSK-A63`, `Custom(" Shop pallet ")` is `CUSTOM:Shop pallet`).
+  `ToolComponent::new` stores the canonical form, and `takes` compares
+  canonical forms. An invalid code mates nothing. Thus validation, the
+  text round trip, the component and the fit agree. A strict refusal of
+  a non-canonical typed value was dropped: the parser already accepts
+  the same text in any case, so the typed value follows the same rule.
+- One `ConnectionCode` type serves both sides (ADINTMS and ADINTWS). A
+  parent's workpiece side and a child's machine side then compare
+  directly. The text form is our own (`BT40`, `HSK-A63`, `ER32`,
+  `CYL 12`, `WELDON 12`, `RECT 25x25`, `CUSTOM:<name>`). Sizes must be in
+  the published series, so a typo such as `BT45` is refused.
+- Coupling rule: the same code fits, with diameters within the holder
+  library's `BORE_SLACK` (0.02 mm). A plain bore or a collet also takes a
+  Weldon shank of its size. A Weldon bore takes only a Weldon shank,
+  because its screw needs the flat.
+- Insert rule, in this order: shape, clearance, size code, thickness (only
+  when the seat states one), clamping against the fixing hole, hand. A
+  neutral insert, or one that states no hand, fits each hand of holder. A
+  handed insert must match the seat's hand. The tolerance class is not
+  checked.
+- Clamping against fixing: C takes an insert with no hole. M, P and D take
+  a cylindrical hole. S takes a countersunk hole. A special fixing (X)
+  fits no standard clamp.
+- The ISO 1832 parser reads the metric layout only. An inch code is too
+  short for it and is refused by name. Position 7 is a nose radius, a
+  sharp corner (`00`), a round insert (`M0`, or `00` on shape R), or a
+  milling wiper facet (two letters). What follows position 7 is kept as
+  written. The hand is read from it only in the plain forms (`R`, or an
+  edge letter and then `R`/`L`/`N`).
+- The inscribed circle is derived from the shape: each edge is the sum of
+  the two tangent lengths `r / tan(a / 2)` at its corners. The size code
+  is the edge cut to whole mm after 0.02 mm, so a 6.35 mm triangle (edge
+  10.998 mm) reads as `11`. Parallelograms, rectangles and round inserts
+  get no inscribed circle.
+- The "round trip" of the model is through its text: an insert code, a
+  holder code and a connection code each parse back to the same value.
+  No serde derive was added: `Tool` has none, and the file format belongs
+  to #3645.
+
+**Why.** The issue asks for a pure model in `camcraft-tools` with named
+refusals. The rules above are general machining practice; the code
+tables are the ones tool vendors publish in their catalogs. No standard
+text is copied.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+- Serde on the components now. Dropped: #3645 owns the
+  `camcraft-components/1` format and its version rules.
+- A collet range on an ER chuck's workpiece side (as the built-in holder
+  library does). Dropped: in the component model the collet is its own
+  component, so the chuck takes an `ER<n>` collet and the collet takes the
+  shank.
+- An ISO 6261 boring bar code parser. Dropped: not in the issue. A boring
+  bar's seat can be made directly as an `InsertSeatSpec`.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Low. Nothing outside the new files reads the
+model yet. A changed rule changes the pinning tests in
+`component_fit_tests.rs` and `insert_designation_tests.rs`.
